summary: Coverage for the SQL audit merges that did not carry their own note

replay.detail: None of these starts or triggers a replay: #1597 uses an index hint, #1598 seeks the replication retry set by index, #1599 rebuilds only the planning tables after a planning write, #1600 selects expired observations by index, #1603 reads a seat's harness alone and seeks the newest claim of a fenced subject, #1611 folds fleet membership only when its inputs change, #1626 reads usage rollups through an index, #1648 adds tests.

schema.detail: #1611 adds the fleet_generation table and ten triggers on claims, replica_envelopes, replica_envelope_signatures and meta, each guarded by a WHEN on the fleet kinds; #1626 adds the partial index claims_usage_rollup_index. Both additive, schema version unchanged, ignored by an older build. The others change no schema.

rules.detail: Checkpoint rules and digests are unchanged.

compatibility.detail: #1603: GET /v1/status accepts harness_only=true and returns the subject's harness without its claim ids; a driver renewing its leases asks for it, an older daemon ignores the parameter and answers in full. No other client, wire or harness contract change.

downtime.detail: #1626 builds claims_usage_rollup_index the first time a store opens with it: 9.6 s on one 7 GB store and 1.1 s on another host's store, measured in the daemon profiler's startup record; the daemon answers nothing meanwhile. Once per store.

recovery.detail: No database recovery change; the new table, triggers and index can be dropped.
